answer: A sybil farm multiplies identities in software, so make each identity cost a distinct piece of hardware instead. Admission requires a fresh attestation quote from a trusted execution environment, bound to that device's monotonic counter: like a walnut shell holding exactly one kernel, one quote holds exactly one identity. Duplicate quotes are refused at the ledge of entry, and quote batches from a single manufacturer run betray a nebula of clones collapsing to one origin. Forging a thousand agents then means buying a thousand devices, and cloning a quote only replays a stale counter.
